question.text: Saraswati Distressed Opportunities Fund, a Cat I AIF, is considering whether to register itself under a specific sub-category of Cat I AIF to act as a Resolution Applicant under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. Which sub-category must the fund register under?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.1.2 (Special Situations Debt as per AIF Regulations), a Special Situation Fund is a sub-category under Category I AIF that invests in special situation assets and may act as a resolution applicant under the IBC, 2016. Other Cat I sub-categories (Infra, SME, VC, Social) cannot act as resolution applicants under IBC. The Trap: Infrastructure and SME Funds are Cat I sub-categories but have separate investment mandates. VC Fund invests in early-stage companies, not stressed assets. None of these can be resolution applicants under IBC. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests Cat I sub-categories at product level. XIX-C tests the regulatory scope — which sub-category unlocks which specific right, such as IBC resolution applicant status. Manager's Pro-Tip: If you anticipate acquiring control of an IBC admitted company, register the AIF specifically as a Special Situation Fund at the outset — re-registration mid-stream is time-consuming and may cause the fund to miss the IBC resolution timeline.
